setup.step12.p: The first screen will ask you to set a password for the built-in "admin" account — this one-time step is called activation. Use at least 8 characters with a mix of upper-case letters, lower-case letters, and numbers. Type it a second time to confirm it matches, then tap or click Activate or OK.

help.q5.p1: No daily maintenance is normally needed. If the Access Point ever needs to move to a new spot, repeat Part 2 and Part 3 above in its new location. If just the Wi-Fi name or password needs to change, log back in and repeat Part 4 (Steps 10–15).

setup.step7.p: Skip this step if you're using PoE only. If a separate power adapter came in the box, plug its small round end into the Access Point's power port, then plug the other end — the brick — into a normal wall outlet, the same kind you'd use for a phone charger.

power.intro: Every Access Point needs power to turn on. There are two different ways to supply it — you only need to use one. Check what's in your box, or ask your manager or IT support if you're not sure which one applies to your store.
setup.step10.p: If you're using the app on your phone, your phone should already be on the store's normal Wi-Fi. If you're using a browser on a computer, that computer should be plugged into the same network as the Access Point — ask IT if you're not sure.

setup.step1.detail: What's usually inside: the Access Point itself (a round disc or a flat panel), a mounting bracket or plate, a small bag of screws, a printed Quick Start sheet (sometimes with a QR code on it) — and in some boxes, a power adapter (a black plug-in brick).
setup.step19.p: If a mounting bracket was included, attach the Access Point to its final position now, following the bracket instructions from the box. Keep the box, spare screws, and Quick Start sheet somewhere safe — and store that password from Step 12 where your team can find it later.

setup.step3.p: Somewhere on the device there's a tiny hole, smaller than a pinhole in a lock. That's the reset button. It needs a pin or an unfolded paperclip to press. You won't need it today — it's only for the "forgot password" situation covered later in Common problems.
setup.step13.p: Look for a menu — usually a list of words down the side of the screen, or three lines/dots (☰) in a corner. Tap or click it, then look for something called Wireless, Wi-Fi, or WLAN Settings.
glossary.intro: A quick reference for terms used in this guide — and terms you might see on the setup screen.
setup.step2.p: A port is just a small doorway that a cable plugs into. Turn the device over, or look along its edge, and you'll see one or two small rectangular slots — sometimes with a tiny label next to them like PoE, LAN, or a little plug icon.
setup.step5.p: Hold the plug so the little clip faces the same way as the port's opening. Push it straight in — not at an angle — into the port marked PoE or LAN from Step 2. Push until you feel or hear a small click.
gl.ap.def: The device this guide is about. Spreads a Wi-Fi signal around a space.
setup.step4.p: This is the main cable you'll need either way. It looks like a slightly thicker phone-charger cable. Both ends have the same clear plastic plug (called an RJ45 connector) with a small plastic clip on top.
overview.calloutP: Think of it like a small radio tower for your store's internet. The internet arrives through a wire; the Access Point broadcasts it through the air.
overview.p1: An Access Point (AP) takes the internet connection coming into your store through a cable and turns it into a wireless Wi-Fi signal. Phones, tablets, laptops, and payment terminals can then connect to that signal without any cables of their own.

setup.step1.p: Take everything out and lay it on the table. Don't throw any small parts away, even ones you don't recognize — they're all meant to be there.

overview.p2: An Access Point is not the same as a router. The router brings the internet into the building and manages the network. The Access Point just spreads the Wi-Fi signal further, so more of the store gets a good signal.
help.q3.p2: If the device is already in use by the store, contact IT before resetting it, since it will disconnect anyone using that Wi-Fi.
setup.step17.p: Type the password exactly as set in Step 15, then tap Join or Connect. Wait a few seconds for a checkmark or a "Connected" label to appear.
setup.step12.detail: Write this password down somewhere safe right now, before moving on. You'll need it again any time you come back to change settings.
power.poe.p1: A single network (Ethernet) cable carries both the internet connection and electrical power at the same time. You plug that one cable into the Access Point, and the other end into a PoE network switch or a PoE injector.

setup.intro: This is the longer, detailed version — every small action is spelled out, so nothing is left to guess. Follow it in order, from top to bottom. It takes about 15–20 minutes and works the same way for all 8 supported models.
help.q3.p1: Most Access Points have a small, recessed reset button that needs a pin to press. Holding it for about 10 seconds resets the device to factory settings — you'll then need to set it up again starting from Step 6.

power.adapter.p1: A power adapter (a plug that goes into a wall outlet) supplies electricity through its own cable. A second, separate Ethernet cable carries the internet connection. Both need to be connected for the device to work.
setup.step18.p: Open any browser app and try loading a website. If a page loads normally, everything is working — setup is complete. If nothing loads, see Common problems below.
gl.router.def: The device that brings the internet into the building and manages the network. Different from an Access Point.

setup.step7.detail: Only use the adapter that came in this exact box. A different adapter — even one that looks similar — can damage the device.
setup.step9.p: Set a timer if that helps. Don't unplug or move anything during this time, even if nothing seems to be happening. When the light settles into a steady pattern — solid, or a slow, even blink rather than a fast one — it's ready for the next part.

footer.safety: Safety first. Always follow your store's electrical safety guidance when plugging in equipment. If anything feels unsafe — exposed wires, a hot device, a burning smell — unplug it and contact IT or facilities immediately.
model6.bestFor: Best for: outdoor coverage — parking lots, exterior entrances, curbside pickup, or loading docks. Never swap its power adapter with an indoor model's.
setup.step16.p: On a phone, open Settings → Wi-Fi. Look through the list for the name you typed in Step 14, and tap it.
